d65br.lane: capx D65-B-R — the coupled arming (Act A + Act B) batch
d65br.authority: owner ruling Q47; r#48 §3(a) gates; r#51 §3(b) adjudication
d65br.gates: The retrofit gates CLEAR — G1′ 1.2898–1.3930 inside MISO's own D64 band 1.26–1.39, G5′ under every ceiling, G2′ exact. G4′ FIRED (I3 unserved/dump PASS → FAIL, I14 PASS → WARN), reported as fired and NOT declared passed — but provably not the two acts': I3 fails starting in 2026 and apply_ccs_retrofit returns at year < ccs_retrofit_available_year (2028) before reading either field, with G0′ independently measuring 0 retrofit rows in 2026 and 2027. The cause is the demand vintage, pre-registered as a confound before the batch ran (D65-B §5 consequence 2 names 2ef4326e (miso) as one of four pre-hunk ISOs).
d65br.g5prime_ruling: Director adjudication r#51 §3(b) (capx-director-ledger-2026-08.md §0av): the CAP-BOUND form of G5′ ('STOP if the cap does NOT bind in a year') is VOID as a STOP and RECLASSIFIED to REPORTED, on the documents — D64 §2.3 says verbatim 'a year converting materially below the cap would be the informative surprise, not a STOP', so the source had already decided this outcome was reported, and Addendum C promoted §2.4's hour-ceiling census cell into a floor on a solved quantity. The CEILING form on ercot/pjm/miso is untouched — a published ceiling is a legitimate upper bound.
d65br.mechanism_reading: Host exhaustion, predicted by k and by nothing else. Both RGGI ISOs start cap-bound at MW-weighted k ≈ 1.0 and unbind exactly as the surviving host pool moves past k > 1.2 (NEISO 0.9952 → 1.3032; NYISO 1.0544 → 1.2235), while CAISO — the third carbon-priced ISO, armed identically — never leaves k 1.03–1.08 and stays cap-bound (96.4 % in 2030). CAISO is the CONTROL CASE: the efficient hosts are consumed first and the expensive tail cannot carry the accurate per-tonne cost, so the unbinding is a fleet-composition effect, not a level effect and not an ISO quirk.
